clue.text: Incorrect kit means trouble

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so the letters of kit and means are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A broken set of equipment is going to cause problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' reads as a noun in the surface but works as a verb telling you to stir up KIT and MEANS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistaken and incorrect are synonyms, both describing something wrong.

clue.text: Threaten one politician with death

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
MP stands for Member of Parliament
death is the end of life

explanation.surface: A lone politician is menaced with being killed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that impends hangs over you as a looming threat, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Projected through sound

indicators.note: the word sound tells the solver to go by how the neighbouring word is spoken

parts.note: taken as written; it is the word said aloud

explanation.surface: Something was beamed out by means of noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a noun meaning noise, but it is the signal that a word is heard rather than seen.
explanation.definitionFit: To project something is to throw or hurl it, so projected is the past tense synonym.

clue.text: General stew thickener

indicators.note: a stew is a jumbled mixture, so the letters of thickener are mixed up

explanation.surface: A cook looks for a sauce thickener for the stew.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Kitchener was a famous British general of the First World War recruiting posters.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitchener was a senior British army officer, so the clue gives an example of the rank.

clue.text: Beginning the Northern climb

parts.note: an ascent is a climb upwards

explanation.surface: A mountaineer starts the climb on the northern face.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nascent is just coming into existence, at its start.

clue.text: Pub arranged to have meals in every bar

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of pub are put in a different order

parts.note: to have meals is to eat

explanation.surface: A pub has been set up so diners can eat at every bar counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' means a pub counter in the surface but a musical measure in the definition: the upbeat is the unaccented beat ending each measure.
explanation.definitionFit: In music the upbeat is the weak beat that recurs within each measure, so it turns up in every one.

clue.text: Not above using two foreign articles

parts.note: un is French for a, the indefinite article
der is German for the, the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone claims to be above using a pair of overseas articles.
explanation.definitionFit: Below is the opposite of above, and below is a synonym of beneath.

clue.text: Take offensive action in two ways, producing great surprise

parts.note: to bomb is to attack from the air
to shell is to attack with artillery fire

explanation.surface: An army attacks on two fronts and stuns the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in two ways' tells you the same phrase is to be read twice, as two different kinds of attack.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of news that shocks everyone is called this, from the image of an explosive shell landing.

clue.text: Make it known the girl's gained little weight

parts.note: Ann is a typical girl's name, and the 's means has
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: Someone declares that a young woman has put on a bit of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce is to proclaim or declare publicly.

clue.text: Demon drink?

definitions.meaning: an evil supernatural being, a ghost or sprite
strong distilled alcohol such as whisky or gin

explanation.surface: Alcohol is the work of the devil, says a temperance campaigner.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a supernatural being and a distilled liquor such as whisky.

clue.text: Tides ebb about workers seeking alluvial deposit

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece wraps round the other
an ebbing tide flows back, so the word tides is read backwards

parts.note: men is a common crossword word for workers

explanation.surface: Receding tides surround labourers searching for river silt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ebb' (the tide flowing back) signals the reversal and 'about' the wrapping; 'Tides' looks like part of a seaside scene but is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Silt and mud laid down by rivers is alluvium, which settles out as sediment.

clue.text: Sole assistance for those travelling in the Arctic

definitions.text: Sole assistance for those travelling in the Arctic

parts.words: Sole assistance for those travelling in the Arctic
parts.note: the only help for polar travellers, or rather a help for the soles of their feet on snow

explanation.surface: Polar explorers have just one source of help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' looks like 'only', but it is the underside of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad frame strapped under a boot spreads the walker's weight over deep powder.

clue.text: Possibly secure and free from danger

indicators.note: possibly signals that secure may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Something might be made safe and released from peril.
explanation.definitionFit: To rescue someone is to save them from harm.

clue.text: What an MP stands for

parts.note: looks like a question about the letters of an abbreviation, but means the district a member of parliament is elected to represent

explanation.surface: A quiz asks what the letters MP abbreviate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stands for' suggests an abbreviation; here it means stands for election in, represents.
explanation.definitionFit: A British parliamentary member represents an electoral district and its voters.

clue.text: It may be tipped but not recommended by doctors

definitions.text: It may be tipped but not recommended by doctors

parts.words: It may be tipped but not recommended by doctors
parts.note: something tipped sounds like a racing tip that experts back, but this tip is a filter on a smoke that doctors warn against

explanation.surface: A racing tip that medical experts would not endorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped' suggests a tipster's recommendation, but means filter-tipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Smokes often have a filter tip, and medical advice warns against smoking.

clue.text: Metal key used by the cook

definitions.text: Metal key used by the cook

parts.note: tin is a metal
a key is something that opens

explanation.surface: A cook carries a key made of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: A tin is the British word for a can, so this kitchen tool opens cans.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen gadget that opens cans of food, a can being a metal container.

clue.text: Childlike woman's body writhing in the dance

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: writhing means twisting about, so the letters of body are twisted

explanation.surface: A girlish woman's figure squirms on the dancefloor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writhing' is the anagram signal and 'in' puts that jumble inside the dance; 'baby doll' is also a short nightdress style.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes a woman who looks or acts like a young girl, as well as a short nightdress.

clue.text: It cannot safely be ignored

parts.note: a riddle about something you disregard at your peril, namely a warning sign

explanation.surface: Some matter must not be overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: A warning sign or light is placed to alert people to a hazard, so overlooking it is risky.

clue.text: Vet gets bug out of parrot's head

indicators.note: gets means the bug takes in another piece inside itself

parts.note: a bug is an insect

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A vet removes a bug from a parrot's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' looks like the animal doctor in the scene, but is the verb meaning examine.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet something is to examine it carefully.

clue.text: Wrongs, a source of Shakespearian comedy

definitions.meaning: Shakespeare wrote The Comedy of ..., so this word is where that comedy comes from

explanation.surface: Mistakes are the basis of humour in Shakespeare's plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistakes are wrongs, and Shakespeare's farce about twins is titled The Comedy of Errors.

clue.text: Why brides may conceal having mixed parentage

indicators.note: conceal means the letters are tucked away inside the words why brides

explanation.surface: Brides keep their mixed family background secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossbred plant or animal, with parents of different kinds, is so described.

clue.text: Sailor died a dissolute man

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees
a rake is a debauched, immoral man

explanation.surface: A seaman died a wastrel.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Francis Drake was a famous Elizabethan English sea captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Drake was a celebrated English seafarer, so the clue names him by his calling.

clue.text: His paper turned to stone

indicators.note: turned means the letters of his paper are turned around into another order

explanation.surface: A man's newspaper became rock-hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue gemstone, the precious kind used in jewellery.

clue.text: He will shortly ring-for your reply

parts.note: taken as written
will shortened is 'll, as in he'll
the letter O is round like a ring

explanation.surface: A man promises to phone soon and await your answer.
explanation.walkthrough: When the phone rings, the greeting you give as you pick up is this word.
explanation.definitionFit: The usual word you say answering the telephone is a greeting reply.

clue.text: After which the participants come out of their shells

definitions.text: After which the participants come out of their shells

parts.words: After which the participants come out of their shells
parts.note: sounds like animals hatching, but the shells are light racing boats that rowers climb out of after the Oxford and Cambridge contest

explanation.surface: Creatures emerge from their shells once an event is over.
explanation.walkthrough: A shell is a light racing rowing boat; the Oxford v Cambridge race on the Thames is famous in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowing contests use slender craft called shells, which crews leave at the finish.

clue.text: Famous London columnist

parts.note: looks like a newspaper writer but is the admiral whose statue tops the column in Trafalgar Square

explanation.surface: A well-known journalist writes for a capital newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson's Column in Trafalgar Square, London, carries a statue of Admiral Nelson.
explanation.definitionFit: The admiral stands atop a tall monument in central London, so he is literally on a column.

clue.text: Maintain there's some body in the beer

indicators.note: in places the body part inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a leg is one part of the body

explanation.surface: Someone claims a corpse has been found in the beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some body' reads as somebody or a corpse, but means a part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert or claim something, to maintain it.

clue.text: He won the race, we hear by a hair's breadth?

definitions.text: He won the race, we hear by a hair's breadth?

parts.words: He won the race, we hear by a hair's breadth?
parts.note: in Aesop's fable the slow creature beat the hare, and hair's breadth sounds like hare's breadth

explanation.surface: A runner is said to have won the race by the narrowest margin.
explanation.walkthrough: In the fable, a hare races a slow shelled reptile and loses; hair is a pun on hare.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop's slow shelled reptile beat the boastful hare in the famous fable.
